review_candidates.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
review_candidates.description: About Metroscope Metroscope builds AI software for power plants. Our products help plant teams turn operational data into decisions: understand performance losses, detect abnormal behavior early, forecast capacity, analyze transient events and explore plant data. Two major product directions are our One Stop Shop vision, connecting these capabilities into a more integrated offering, and the integration of agentic AI into our products. Product Marketing sits at the intersection of Product, Sales, Marketing and the field. Our users and buyers are technical. Credibility comes from understanding the product and their reality, not only from producing marketing assets. The role We are looking for a Product Marketing Manager who can take ownership of an evolving scope and focus on what matters most for the business. You will report directly to the CPMO. What you will focus on Market understanding and positioning. Understand customer needs, market dynamics and competitors to identify opportunities and apply and refine our existing positioning where needed. Go-to-market strategy and execution. Drive product and feature launches, support growth within existing accounts and into new markets, and contribute to partnership initiatives through launch plans and cross-functional coordination. Sales enablement and adoption. Master our existing material, improve decks, demos and use cases with support from Ops on technical content, train Sales, join customer conversations and make sure the assets we build are actually used. Product Marketing operating model. Help the team stabilize simple and useful ways of working across insights, launches, enablement and feedback loops. How we expect you to work Go deep enough into the product to discuss it credibly with Product, Ops, Sales and technical customers. Spend time understanding how people actually work in power plants and what matters to them. Start from the business problem, not from a predefined Product Marketing framework. Prefer a useful first version and fast learning over waiting for perfect information. Stay hands-on. You should be comfortable creating and editing slides, working in Figma or Canva, updating Webflow, using Notion, LLMs or any tool you will need to help you optimize your work. Build trust by delivering, listening and following through. What success looks like after 6-12 months Sales understand, trust and use the Product Marketing material. You have built a direct understanding of our users, products and market. The core PMM processes are simple, stable and do not depend on one person remembering everything. Sales can confidently present and demonstrate our products using relevant use cases and evidence of customer value. Product Marketing supports launches and growth opportunities with clear, practical material that teams actually use. What we are looking for We are looking for seniority in judgment, ownership and execution , more than a specific number of years. You will likely have: Strong Product Marketing experience in B2B SaaS or another complex technical product environment. Evidence that you have worked closely with Sales and Product and owned initiatives from diagnosis to delivery and adoption. The ability to understand technical subjects and turn them into clear customer and business value. Fluency in French, in addition to strong written and verbal communication skills in English. The autonomy to move forward in an environment where priorities evolve and not everything is defined upfront. Experience in energy, industrial software or an engineering environment is a plus, but curiosity and the ability to learn the domain deeply matter more. Workplace and benefits This is a permanent position based in Paris, with remote work a few days per week. The expected start is in 2027. 75% of your Navigo public transport pass covered by Metroscope, or a sustainable mobility allowance of up to €700 per year. Swile meal card: €10 per day, with 60% covered by Metroscope. Alan health insurance, with 70% covered by Metroscope. €300 for your remote work setup. EDF Group savings plan with employer matching contributions. Profit-sharing agreement of up to 10% of fixed salary. Team-building events and company seminars. 📞 Screening A first conversation about your motivation, understanding of the role, expectations and practical details. ⚙️ Round 2 - Technical interview (2h) Technical interview with Youssef and Sylvain, that will include a case study. 📸 Round 3 - HR and Fit (2h) Meet fellow team members, HR and our CEO on this final round.

review_candidates.title: Senior Event Producer
review_candidates.location: WP. Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
review_candidates.description: Senior Event Producer We are a specialist financial publishing, events and intelligence business seeking an experienced and highly capable Senior Event Producer to join our team.   Our events bring together senior figures from across the financial services industry, including regulators, financial institutions, investors, professional advisers and other industry leaders. The role spans three principal formats: international forums and conferences, invitation-only roundtables and dialogues, and specialist training programmes.   This is primarily a content and programme production role, rather than an event logistics position. The successful candidate will take significant responsibility for what our events discuss, who participates and how those discussions are developed. Remuneration: RM4000 - RM6000   The Role The Senior Event Producer will play a central role in the development and quality of our international events programme.   Responsibilities will include: Researching markets, industry developments and emerging themes to identify relevant and commercially attractive event topics. Developing agendas, session concepts and programme content across conferences, roundtables, dialogues and training programmes. Identifying, approaching and securing high-quality speakers, moderators and contributors. Building and maintaining relationships with senior industry participants, including regulators, financial institutions, investors, advisers and other key stakeholders. Working directly with speakers and moderators in the lead-up to events to ensure sessions are well structured, relevant and engaging. Developing detailed session plans, including discussion themes, questions and briefing materials for moderators and panellists. Identifying new speakers, organisations and perspectives rather than relying solely on established industry contacts. Contributing ideas for new event formats, markets and subject areas and helping continuously improve existing programmes. Working closely with colleagues across the business to ensure programmes meet both editorial and commercial objectives. Taking ownership of projects and deadlines, anticipating potential issues and ensuring that commitments are followed through. Working closely with our events team to ensure programme and speaker requirements are communicated effectively ahead of each event. Attending selected international events and supporting speakers, moderators and programme delivery on-site where required.   The role also includes responsibility for the accurate and timely coordination of programme-related materials, including speaker biographies, presentation materials, moderator briefings, training documentation and other event content.   The Person This role requires considerably more than good organisation. We are looking for someone with judgement, intellectual curiosity, confidence and a strong sense of ownership.   You will ideally have at least two years' experience producing high-quality conferences, roundtables, training programmes or other business events, with a demonstrable record of developing strong programmes and securing senior speakers. Experience in financial services, professional services or another sophisticated B2B sector would be a significant advantage.   You will be able to work independently and make good decisions without requiring constant direction. You will be comfortable taking responsibility for a programme or project and driving it forward from initial research and concept development through to the event itself.   You will have excellent written and spoken English and the ability to research unfamiliar subjects, understand them quickly and turn that research into intelligent programme content and discussion topics.   You will also be confident communicating with senior industry figures. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable approaching a prospective speaker for the first time, developing a relationship with a regulator or senior executive, and working closely with moderators and panellists to improve the quality of a discussion.   We particularly value people who are naturally curious and proactive: someone who asks what could be done better, spots opportunities and problems early, and acts rather than waiting to be instructed. You will be highly organised, commercially aware, entrepreneurial and comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities can change. You should enjoy being part of a small team in which people take responsibility and contribute beyond narrowly defined job descriptions.   International travel will be required.   An understanding of modern research tools and the use of AI and other technologies for research, programme development and productivity is essential.

review_candidates.title: Production Manager
review_candidates.description: Job description Production Manager Fashion – Megan Salmon Pty Ltd Oct 6, 2026 · start date- End November 2026 About the role Position: Production Manager Employment type: Full time Reports to: Designer / Creative Director Megan Salmon is an acclaimed women's fashion label based in Fremantle WA well-known for original prints, quality textiles, superb make-quality and a wide size range. The label produces 2 seasons a year of 100+ styles , plus regular capsule injections. The business comprises strong and growing on-line sales, wholesale accounts across Australia and NZ and 2 shops, Fremantle and Melbourne. Our garment production is in Vietnam, Bali and China, and we also produce textiles featuring Megan Salmon designs. All stock is delivered to and inventory is then managed and dispatched from the Fremantle site. We are a small highly capable agile team. The business is 100% owned and operated by Megan Salmon.  The Position We are seeking an outstanding and experienced Production Manager to take charge all aspects of the production processes, from manufacturing our own print textiles, sourcing other fabric, to design concepts, through to finished garments. You will work side-byside with the designer to bring each collection to life, managing every step from sample ranges through to bulk production and delivery. We are seeking someone who is highly capable, enthusiastic, excellent communicator and problem solver, clear thinking, highly numerate with outstanding IT skills and is a superior project manager. Someone who enjoys responsibility and is simply a great colleague. You will be the central point of contact for our three overseas manufacturing partners and responsible for keeping quality, cost and timelines on track. You will be required to visit Bali and Vietnam for sample range handover and confirm each season’s production program. You will also manage stock replenishment and reorders so our best-selling styles stay in stock. The positon supervises a Production Assistant who is reponsible for assembling Tech Packs and other other tasks. Key responsibilitiesProduct development and sampling •        Work closely with the designer from concept to final sample, and supervise tech packs and specifications. •        Assemmbletrims lists, measurement specs and grading for suppliers. •        Manage the full sampling process: proto, fit, salesman and pre-production samples. •        Run fit sessions with the designer, r and implement amendments •        Source and approve fabrics, trims, prints, lab dips and strike-offs. Bulk production •        Place and manage bulk purchase orders across Vietnam, Bali and China. •        Build and maintain the critical path for each collection, tracking every milestone from sample to delivery. •        Monitor production progress and flag delays early, with solutions to protect launch dates. •        Approve pre-production samples, size sets and top-of-production samples before bulk proceeds. •        Coordinate freight, shipping and customs documentation with logistics partners. Supplier management •        Act as the main point of contact for all manufacturing partners across the three regions. •        Negotiate pricing, minimum order quantities and lead times. •        Allocate styles to the most suitable supplier based on capability, cost and capacity. •        Assess supplier performance and source new partners when needed. Stock replenishment and reorders •        Review sell-through and stock levels with the team to identify styles for reorder. •        Place replenishment and reorder purchase orders in time to avoid stock-outs. •        Manage reorder lead times and fabric availability, including holding greige or core fabrics where useful. •        Keep consistent quality and fit across repeat production runs. Quality Control, costing and compliance •        Manage QC program, Set and uphold quality standards, managing inspections and resolving faults with suppliers. •        Prepare product costings and work to target margins with the designer. •        Keep accurate records of orders, approvals, costings and production data. •        Ensure suppliers meet ethical sourcing, labelling and compliance requirements. Skills and experience •        At least 5 years' production experience in women's fashion, with 2 or more years in a production manager or senior production role. •        Proven experience managing offshore manufacturing, ideally in Vietnam, Bali (Indonesia) and/or China. •        Strong garment construction knowledge across wovens and knits, plus fabrics, trims and finishes. •        Confident reading and writing tech packs, specs and grading. •        Solid understanding of costing, critical paths, MOQs and lead times. •        Experience with stock replenishment, reorders and working from sell-through data. •        Good working knowledge of freight, shipping and import processes. •        Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills; experience with Cin 7 i Or similar •        Tertiary qualification in fashion, textiles or production is desirable. About you •        Highly organised, able to juggle several collections, suppliers and time zones at once. •        A clear, calm communicator who builds trust with designers and factories alike. •        A sharp eye for detail, fit and finish, with a genuine passion for beautiful product. •        Proactive problem solver who spots issues early and acts before they become delays. •        Commercially minded, balancing design vision with cost, quality and timelines. •        Available to travel overseas when needed. What we offer •        A full-time role at the heart of a design-led 100% Australian women's fashion label. •        Close collaboration with the designer and real ownership of the production process. •        Opportunity to travel to and work with our partners in Vietnam, Bali and China. •        Salary: 85-100k Location: Fremantle, WA Job summaryMegan Salmon (Fremantle) seeks a Production Manager, $85-100k, to run design-to-delivery across Vietnam, Bali & China. 5+ yrs fashion experience. Key selling points Work side by side with the designer and own production from concept to garment. Travel to build strong relationships with factories in Vietnam, Bali and China. Earn $85-100k at a design-led women's fashion label in beautiful Fremantle, WA.

review_candidates.title: Operations Manager, Global Strategic Accounts
review_candidates.description: About the Role The Operations Manager, Global Strategic Accounts oversees the day-to-day delivery of a large global enterprise account. This full-time role manages a distributed team of Wellbeing Coordinators and directs the work of contract Health Coaches assigned to the account. Working remotely in the United States, the Operations Manager enables coordinators and coaches to execute campaigns, live sessions, and other program activities across global regions. This role establishes clear expectations, resolves operational issues, and maintains consistent quality while accommodating local needs. The Operations Manager partners closely with the Program Manager on delivery plans and capacity, the Account Director on account priorities and escalations, and the Director of Coaching Operations on coaching standards and quality. While the Program Manager owns program scope and delivery timelines, the Operations Manager owns delivery execution, staffing assignments, and team capacity. Key Responsibilities Lead the global delivery team by hiring, onboarding, managing, and developing Wellbeing Coordinators, establishing clear expectations, providing regular feedback, and addressing performance concerns. Direct contract coaches day-to-day by setting program goals, defining success metrics, providing clear guidance on live events, and aligning coach activities with account strategy. Assign and schedule coaches across one-on-one coaching, live sessions, and fitness classes. Conduct regular team meetings and individual check-ins with coordinators and coaches. Manage workloads, coverage, and areas of specialty across multiple regions and time zones. Establish and uphold delivery standards for how events, outreach, and results are scheduled, tracked, and reported across all regions. Oversee the execution of campaigns, webinars, events, employee communications, coaching, and community activities. Translate program roadmaps into regional delivery plans, operational priorities, and measurable goals. Develop and maintain templates, checklists, playbooks, and operating procedures used by coordinators to prepare and run scheduled activities. Track team availability, coaching utilization, and upcoming delivery commitments to support capacity planning. Record delivered activities against contracted commitments and provide operational data for client reviews. Monitor regional performance across activity types, determine regional programming mix within the roadmap, and recommend roadmap adjustments when appropriate. Maintain operational trackers and coordinate access to internal and client systems with IT and Security teams. Manage day-to-day relationships and budgets for coaching vendors and contractors in partnership with People and Legal teams, ensuring work remains within contracted scope. Monitor service quality, participant feedback, and operational metrics, collaborating with internal leadership to resolve recurring issues and enhance delivery workflows. Exercise decision rights over coach and coordinator assignments, scheduling, regional programming mix, and delivery process changes, while escalating scope, budget, or headcount changes to the Account Director. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university. 5+ years of experience in program or service delivery operations. 3+ years of direct people management experience. Ability to consistently work hours that overlap with EMEA and APAC teams. Proven experience leading and developing a distributed team across multiple regions and time zones. Demonstrated experience overseeing ongoing client programs involving multiple activities, stakeholders, and delivery commitments. Experience coordinating contractors or specialized service providers while managing team coverage and capacity. Demonstrated ability to develop clear delivery processes, quality standards, and escalation paths. Experience using service data and participant feedback to resolve operational challenges and improve delivery performance. Compensation and Benefits Expected base salary range: $130,000 - $160,000 per year, dependent on factors such as experience and expertise. Eligibility for performance bonus and equity. Comprehensive health coverage, including medical, dental, and vision insurance. 401(k) retirement plan with organization match. Paid time off. Equal Opportunity Employer The organization is committed to creating a safe and welcoming work environment free of discrimination and harassment. Equal employment opportunity is provided to all employees and applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, genetics, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, family or parental status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Reasonable accommodations are available for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans throughout the application and employment process.
